page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.xlarge is an entry-level virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.n4.xlarge operates primarily in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 25% tier. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with read-only bandwidth benchmarks falling into the bottom 25% for both small and large blocks, though large block write bandwidth reaches average levels. Computational tasks such as gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core processing rank in the bottom 10% tier. Database operations and Passmark memory scores also register in the bottom 10%, reflecting significant resource constraints under load.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest hardware specifications, this instance represents a budget-friendly option designed for low-intensity workloads where resource density and cost minimization are prioritized over raw performance. It is suited for lightweight applications such as static web serving, basic development or testing environments, and low-transaction background tasks. It is not recommended for database hosting, high-throughput data processing, or memory-intensive applications due to its low benchmark scores in those areas.
